title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying your coverage will be canceled unless you give them personal or banking information. They may use scare tactics to pressure you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your coverage will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and bank account now."
red_flags: Requests for personal or banking info
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying a package couldn’t be delivered and you need to click a link to reschedule or pay a fee. The link leads to a fake site that steals your information or installs malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to reschedule: [fake link]"
red_flags: Requests for payment or personal info
what_to_do: Delete the text and do not click any links.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails pretending to be from the Social Security Administration. They claim there is a problem with your account and ask you to click a link or call a number to fix it.
example_message: "We noticed suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please verify your information here: [fake link]"
red_flags: Email from 'Social Security' asking for info
what_to_do: Do not click links—go to the official SSA website or call their real number.

title: Facebook 'Friend in Need' Money Request
how_it_works: A scammer hacks a friend’s Facebook account and sends you a message saying they’re in trouble and need money right away. They ask you to send gift cards or wire money.
example_message: "Hi, I’m stuck and need your help. Can you send me a $200 gift card? I’ll pay you back."
red_flags: Urgent money request from a friend
Requests for gift cards or wire transfers
what_to_do: Call your friend directly to check if it’s really them before sending money.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: You get a call from someone pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money for bail or an emergency. They ask you not to tell anyone.
example_message: "Grandma, it’s me. I’m in jail and need you to send money right away. Please don’t tell mom and dad."
red_flags: Caller claims to be a grandchild in trouble
Asks you to keep it secret
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check the story.
